thread:
IncidentBot: Pager triggered for APAC region: apac-east autoscaler thrash + spot GPU preemptions. 65-80% of GPU nodes evicted in last 3m, queue depth rising, latency SLOs breached for some customers. Incident ID INC-2071239.
Nina: I’m on call — joining bridge now. tagging @Sanjay and @Matt for infra and routing.
Sanjay: on it, pulling node events. likely cloud preemption wave. will check node group scaling limits and recent eviction logs.
Matt: I'm here — can we fail traffic to eu-west fallback while we stabilize? routing policy should allow cross-region fallback for premium customers.
SupportBot: Notifying impacted accounts: AcmeCorp (prod), LumenAI (staging). Customer-visible errors: intermittent 503s, higher latency.
Nina: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) engage autoscaler hold (prevent further scale-down) 2) enable cross-region fallback for affected routes 3) spin up reserved dedicated nodes in apac if possible 4) start bridge & postmortem scheduling.
Elaine: I can toggle routing but need confirmation which model variants to route. prefer routing to quantized smaller model on eu-west to keep latency acceptable.
Sanjay: Confirmed preemption pattern: spot evictions across apac-east-1a/b. Cloud provider is reclaiming GPUs. Node scale-up is failing due to limit RL-APAC-GPU-QUOTA.
Devin: I have a temporary quota bump request in flight but will take ~10-15m. meanwhile I can hit the reserved pool and spin up 6x g4dn-equivalent nodes as fallback.
Nina: Devin do that. Matt/ Elaine - start fallback routing immediately for the highest priority routes (prod inference for AcmeCorp). Mark others as degraded.
Matt: Executing route rule change now:
```
# routing change
patch /routes/customer/acmecorp -> region eu-west fallback model: ridge-quant-8b
set priority=high
```
Matt: Done. route update pushed, should take effect in ~30s.
IncidentBot: Alert: Fallback route applied to 3 routes for AcmeCorp.
SupportBot: Sent proactive customer message to AcmeCorp: "We've detected degraded performance and are routing to our eu-west fallback. We're monitoring and will follow up."
Sanjay: Manual blocker: autoscaler controller is in crashloop in apac-east. kubelet logs show OOMs on controller manager. grabbing logs now.
Nina: Assigning roles: Incident lead: Nina, Infra owner: Sanjay, Routing: Matt, Customer comms: Elaine, Capacity follow-up: Devin.
Sanjay: Found root cause for crashloop: controller memory leak after recent release (autoscaler v2.4.1). Stacktrace attached. Will roll back the controller to v2.4.0 as hotfix.
Matt: Rolling back autoscaler deployment to v2.4.0: `kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/autoscaler --to-revision=2`
Matt: Rollback initiated.
IncidentBot: Deployment rollback started at 2071240055.
Sanjay: Controller stabilized after rollback. autoscaler resumed normal activity but nodegroup still under-provisioned due to quota.
Devin: Reserved nodes are up (6 GPUs) and joined cluster. Pod backfills happening. Queue depth dropping.
Nina: Monitoring metrics: token latency back to baseline for routed requests, but some non-routed customers still see elevated latencies. Need to track remediation actions and create Jira tickets.
Elaine: Noted. I’ll open an incident summary for CS and schedule a proactive outreach for impacted customers.
Devin: Quota request approved (temporary bump) but we should not rely on repeats. filing a long-term capacity plan ticket.
Nina: Post-incident next steps: schedule postmortem + assign action items. We should also add an emergency runbook entry for controller rollback and autoscaler hold.
Sanjay: Action item A1: Add memory leak check to CI for autoscaler (owner: Sanjay, ticket RED-4378, due 2027-01-18).
Devin: Action item A2: Create reserved capacity plan for APAC (owner: Devin, ticket RED-4380, due 2027-01-25).
Matt: Action item A3: Update routing fallback docs to permit cross-region fallback for select customers and add automated testing (owner: Matt, ticket RED-4381, due 2027-01-12).
Elaine: Action item A4: Customer comms and RCA draft (owner: Elaine, ticket RED-4382, due 2027-01-10).
Nina: Action item A5: Add canary for autoscaler v2.x releases with memory/heap checks (owner: SRE, ticket RED-4383, due 2027-01-15).
IncidentBot: Postmortem meeting proposed: 2027-01-08 15:00 UTC. Organizer: Nina. Location: #incidents-bridge.
SupportBot: CS outreach scheduled for 2027-01-06 10:00 PST for AcmeCorp and LumenAI.
Sanjay: Notes for postmortem: include heap dump timeline, controller code changes in v2.4.1, and node eviction correlation with provider maintenance windows.
Devin: Long-term: propose reserve pool for critical customers in APAC to avoid spot-only reliance. will include cost estimates in RED-4380.
Matt: I’ll add automated integration test that simulates mass spot preemptions and validates fallback routing executes within 60s.
Elaine: RCA draft snippet for customers: "Root cause: memory leak in autoscaler controller v2.4.1 triggered crashloops under eviction pressure. This caused temporary under-provisioning of GPU nodes while we rolled back the controller and provisioned reserved capacity. Mitigations applied: rollback, reserved nodes, cross-region fallback."
Nina: Closing notes: incident severity lowered to SEV3 at 2071241400. All primary mitigations in place. Will keep monitoring for 24h and update postmortem ticket.
IncidentBot: Incident INC-2071239 status: mitigated -> monitoring.
SupportBot: Follow-ups: flagged impacted customers in CRM, created case numbers CS-9921 (AcmeCorp) and CS-9922 (LumenAI).
Nina: Please update your tickets with progress and link to incident thread. I'll take postmortem notes during the meeting and publish final RCA by 2027-01-12.
Sanjay: Quick commands used:
```
# check node events
kubectl get events -n kube-system --field-selector reason=Evicted
# rollback autoscaler
kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/autoscaler --to-revision=2
# scale reserved pool
gcloud compute instance-groups managed resize apac-reserved-gpu-pool --size=6
```
Matt: Closing the on-call handoff note: next oncall is @Devin at 2071243600 UTC.
Nina: Thanks all — good coordination. will follow up with action-item tracking in RED board. :thumbsup:
